mechanism.summary: Stacked on wide-tier-interpreter-exits and planned from the same queue for a batched promotion. Every exec/test rebuilt its PreparedRegexp from the source text, and every evaluation of a regular-expression literal re-validated its pattern. A realm-owned, bounded cache now shares one compiled program per source and matching-flag set, and remembers validated source/flags pairs; String.prototype.replace's global path uses the same programs. Plan written after one exploratory screen; the target is the queue opportunity whose profile named these costs.
mechanism.generality: Every RegExp object, literal or constructed, with a source seen before in the realm reuses its program; the cache is keyed only by source and flags and holds no objects.
semantic_risks: lastIndex and every other per-object state must stay on the object
Different flag sets over one source must compile separately
An invalid pattern must fail on every construction
Clearing a full table must not change any match result

profile_evidence.shared_cost: Exact queue-candidate binary sampling the official bundle repeated 30 times in one script (one-second window; a single run is shorter than sampler attach). The literal evaluation reaches the RegExp constructor on every loop iteration: construct_function 61 of 982 samples, validate_regexp_init about 29, and every test rebuilds a PreparedRegexp before matching.
